connectors.name: @actiongate/adapters
connectors.summary: Adapters for tool-calling agent loops, plain async functions, and inbound automation webhooks.
connectors.protects: The dispatch path an agent framework, workflow step, or automation platform uses to reach a handler.
bypass: Anything that can call the handler outside this dispatch path is unguarded; the adapter protects the wrapper, not the callee.
An inbound webhook is only as trustworthy as its shared secret; whoever holds that secret can present a valid delivery.
Relayed user intent comes from the model or the automation platform and is evidence only; it can never override a hard rule.
negativeTests: BLOCK, REVIEW, a missing grant, a failed consumption, and an unreachable ActionGate never dispatch
Unknown and disabled tools give an identical refusal, so probing reveals nothing
Malformed tool arguments are refused before any authorization is attempted
A forged, tampered, or replayed webhook is refused before any provider spend

connectors.name: @actiongate/http-proxy
connectors.summary: HTTP reverse proxy and sidecar that maps routes to registry tools and consumes before forwarding.
connectors.protects: The upstream service's network endpoint and its credential, which stay inside the proxy process.
bypass: Anything that can route to the upstream service directly bypasses the proxy; isolation is a network property.
The downstream proxy token is a bearer token and grants that agent's authority until rotation.
Routes that are not declared simply do not exist here, so an unmapped upstream path is unreachable through the proxy but still reachable directly.
negativeTests: An unmapped route is a 404 and never a pass-through
A route whose tool is disabled in the registry never reaches upstream
BLOCK, REVIEW, a missing grant, and a failed consumption never reach upstream
The arguments authorized are the arguments forwarded

connectors.name: @actiongate/mcp-gateway
connectors.summary: Embeddable MCP tool registry that owns tool metadata and consumes before executing.
connectors.protects: In-process MCP tool handlers and the runtime credentials passed to them.
bypass: A handler registered elsewhere in the same process, or exported publicly, can be called without a grant.
The host application can call the raw execute function directly; the gateway only guards its own dispatch path.
negativeTests: An unregistered tool name is rejected before authorization
Mutated arguments fail grant binding and never execute
A replayed grant is rejected and the handler runs exactly once

connectors.name: @actiongate/mcp-proxy
connectors.summary: Standalone MCP network proxy that owns the upstream credential and consumes before forwarding.
connectors.protects: The upstream MCP server's network endpoint and its credential, both of which stay inside the proxy process.
bypass: Anything that can route to the upstream MCP endpoint directly bypasses the proxy entirely; isolation is a network property.
The downstream proxy token is a bearer token, so whoever holds it acts as that agent until rotation.
Relayed user intent is agent-supplied evidence and can influence the semantic signal, though never a hard rule.
negativeTests: An unknown or disabled tool is never forwarded and reveals nothing by its error
BLOCK, REVIEW, a missing grant, and a failed consumption never reach upstream
Unhandled JSON-RPC methods are refused rather than passed through
_meta is stripped before forwarding so a grant cannot be smuggled upstream

connectors.name: @actiongate/sdk
connectors.summary: TypeScript client that authorizes and consumes a grant before calling a private function.
connectors.protects: The application's own tool function, which must stay private to the module that wraps it.
bypass: Any other caller that can reach the same function directly is unguarded; wrapTool protects the wrapper, not the callee.
A downstream credential held by the application rather than the wrapper remains reachable without a grant.
negativeTests: BLOCK and REVIEW never call the wrapped function
A missing grant in enforce mode never calls the wrapped function
A failed consumption never calls the wrapped function

connectors.name: actiongate-python
connectors.summary: Python client that authorizes and consumes a grant before calling a private handler.
connectors.protects: The application's own tool function, which must stay private to the module that wraps it.
bypass: Any other caller that can reach the same function directly is unguarded; wrap_tool protects the wrapper, not the callee.
A downstream credential held by the application rather than the wrapper remains reachable without a grant.
negativeTests: BLOCK and REVIEW never call the handler
A missing grant in enforce mode never calls the handler
A failed consumption never calls the handler
An unreachable API never calls the handler
